spans.note: Results / Relation Between Player Skin Tone and Red Cards Received

spans.assertion: in this variant analysis, player club was excluded as a covariate at the project leaders' request, otherwise identical to the Final Approach
player position was included as a covariate because it significantly related to both skin tone (F=5.33) and red cards (F=8.27)
total games played was included as a potential covariate because it correlated with skin tone (r=-.06) and red cards (r=.40)
player height was included as a potential covariate because it correlated with skin tone (r=-.06) and red cards (r=.07)
red cards significantly correlated with player age (r=.35), player weight (r=.09), and total goals scored (r=.19)
age, weight, and goals scored were consequently also examined as potential covariates
ran a multiple linear regression with total red cards as outcome, average skin tone as main predictor, and all identified variables as covariates, using simultaneous forced-entry
overall model significantly predicted red cards, F(17,1401)=20.37, p<.001, R2=.20
player weight and player height coefficients were not significant (β=.003,p=.93; β=-.044,p=.26)
skin tone had a significant unique relation with red cards after accounting for other predictors, β=.060, p=.02
weight and height were removed from the model due to nonsignificant unique relations
removal of weight and height did not significantly worsen model fit, ΔF(2,1401)=0.95, p=.39
the trimmed final model significantly predicted red cards, F(15,1417)=23.54, p<.001, R2=.20
final model showed a significant unique skin tone-red card relation, β=.062, p=.01
converted the standardized coefficient to Cohen's d = 0.124, 95% CI [0.028, 0.220]
average player skin tone was computed as the arithmetic mean of two research assistants' ratings per player
the two raters' skin-tone ratings were highly correlated (r=.924, p<.001), cited to justify averaging them
player age was calculated using a fixed reference date (01/01/2013) and each player's birthdate
contrast coding (11 contrasts for 12 positions) was used to represent player position, and the same method was used for player club
data were restructured from player-referee dyad rows into one row per player
restructuring reduced the case count from 146,028 player-referee dyads to 2,053 players
per-dyad games-played, goals-scored, and red-card variables were summed across dyads to create total games played, total goals scored, and total red cards received
cases with missing data on the relevant variables were excluded, so sample size and degrees of freedom vary across analyses
the final skin tone-red card regression used 1,433 of 2,053 players (69.8%); exclusions were missing position data (152), skin tone ratings (253), or both (215)
multiple linear regression was chosen to test skin tone against total red cards, with additional covariates considered to isolate a unique relation

used the same scatterplots to visually check homoscedasticity of residuals

authors decided not to be concerned about the heavy-tailed residuals, citing that in large samples nonnormality does not seriously affect significance tests or CIs (Cohen et al., 2003)

spans.assertion: in this alternate implicit-bias analysis, player club was again excluded as a covariate per the project leaders' request
overall model (club excluded) significantly predicted red card received, χ2(17)=1055.82, p<.001, Nagelkerke R2=.07
the implicit-bias by skin-tone interaction did not significantly predict red card received (eβ=0.057, Wald χ2(1)=1.061, p=.30); implicit bias of referee country was not found to moderate the relation
for moderation analyses, data were NOT restructured into one row per player; each case remained a player-referee dyad
per-dyad games-played and goals-scored variables (not the totals) were used in the moderation analyses
number of red cards per dyad was dichotomized (0 = none, 1 = one or more)
only 0.017120% (25 of 146,028) of dyads had more than one red card, cited to justify the dichotomization
implicit bias score and average skin tone were mean-centered, and an interaction term was created by multiplying the two centered variables
missing data were handled by excluding cases missing data on relevant variables

final analysis included 116,014 of 146,028 dyads (79.5%); exclusions were missing position (8,454), skin tone (12,134), implicit bias (146), position+skin tone (9,263), skin tone+implicit bias (8), position+implicit bias (7), all three (2)

binary logistic regression tested implicit bias as a moderator using centered implicit bias, centered skin tone, their interaction, and covariates (position, club, games played, goals scored, age), simultaneous forced entry
overall model was significant, χ2(106)=1282.17, p<.001, Nagelkerke R2=.09
implicit-bias by skin-tone interaction did not significantly predict red card received (eβ=0.329, Wald χ2(1)=0.149, p=.70); implicit bias was not found to moderate the relation
in the initial approach for the implicit-bias model, position contrasts were included/excluded by individual significance; the final approach retained all contrasts
player club was added as a covariate in the final approach only, per reviewer recommendation
country-of-club was removed as a covariate for the final approach per the lead authors' instruction
skin-tone scale was rescaled from 1-5 to 0-1 for the final approach

initial-approach model (implicit-bias) included position (certain contrasts), age, games played, goals scored, country-of-club (certain contrasts), and skin tone; differed from final approach by excluding club, using partial position contrasts, and including some country-of-club contrasts
initial-approach model was significant, χ2(13)=1132.01, p<.001, Nagelkerke R2=.08
implicit-bias by skin-tone interaction was also not significant in the initial approach (eβ=0.937, Wald χ2(1)=0.008, p=.93); not found to moderate
